headline: Autonomous AI agents drove the day's vulnerability research, finding and exploiting fresh zero-days in Redis and NodeBB while Google's CodeMender turned the same automation toward writing patches.

emerging_trends.text: Autonomous agents took over the vulnerability pipeline this week as Kimi K3 agents built working Redis exploits, Aikido's pentest bots cracked NodeBB in six hours, and Google's CodeMender began writing its own patches, research tooling that attackers can wield just as easily.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agents Find and Patch Zero-Days at Scale

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware kept fragmenting into more crews chasing more victims, with 61 new groups surfacing in a year and gangs pushing past hospitals to squeeze the healthcare supply chain and manufacturers running PTC Windchill.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ransomware Market Fragments as Groups Multiply

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep turning trusted identity infrastructure against its owners, and the newly published Certighost exploit shows how a single low-privileged Active Directory account can escalate to domain-wide compromise through certificate services.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Certighost Lets Low-Privilege Users Seize Domain Controllers

topics.title: AI Agents Find and Patch Zero-Days at Scale
topics.latest_developments: Redis shipped seven security releases on July 23 after researchers ran Kimi K3 agents to find memory flaws and build authenticated remote-code-execution proofs across stock Redis 6.2.22, 7.4.9, 8.6.4, and 8.8.0; Aikido Security's AI pentest agents found eight high-severity NodeBB flaws in a six-hour source review; and Google previewed CodeMender, an agent that confirms exploitable bugs and generates fixes.
topics.summary: Researchers and defenders now point autonomous agents at source code to discover, prove, and repair vulnerabilities faster than manual review, a capability that cuts both ways. Redis patched in 6.2.23, 7.2.15, and 7.4.10; NodeBB administrators should run 4.14.2.

sources.title: Kimi K3 Agents Found Redis Zero-Days and Built RCE Exploit, Researchers Say
NodeBB Patches Eight AI-Found Flaws Exposing Admin Access and Private Chats
Google gives developers an AI bug hunter that also writes patches

topics.title: Ransomware Market Fragments as Groups Multiply
topics.latest_developments: Black Kite's 2026 report counted 61 new ransomware groups between April 2025 and March 2026, more than one a month, and Flare's Assaf Morag found gangs hitting EMEA healthcare's suppliers—telemedicine providers and vendors—across the whole ecosystem rather than headline hospital targets alone.
topics.summary: The ransomware market has fragmented as many crews scale playbooks at once and reach deeper into the supply chain. Smaller healthcare vendors now absorb attacks as damaging as those against hospitals.

sources.title: Ransomware in 2026: More groups, more victims, no slowdown
Ransomware gangs go after EMEA healthcare's supply chain

topics.title: Certighost Lets Low-Privilege Users Seize Domain Controllers
topics.latest_developments: Researchers H0j3n and Aniq Fakhrul published a working exploit on July 24 that lets any low-privileged Active Directory user obtain a certificate for a domain controller, authenticate as that machine, and abuse its replication rights to DCSync the krbtgt secret.
topics.summary: Certighost turns an ordinary domain account into full directory compromise through Active Directory Certificate Services. Organizations running AD CS should audit certificate templates and enrollment permissions now.

sources.title: Certighost Exploit Lets Low-Privileged Active Directory Users Impersonate a Domain Controller

topics.title: Azure Automation Default Enables Cross-Tenant Takeover
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft fixed a public-by-default configuration and chain of code flaws in Azure Automation that let an attacker seize another tenant's managed identity and reach its data, credentials, and cloud workloads.
topics.summary: The default Azure Automation setting exposed accounts across tenant boundaries, opening the door to cross-tenant identity theft. Microsoft has remediated the issue; customers should verify their Automation configurations.

sources.title: Default Azure Automation Setting Enables Cross-Tenant Identity Takeover

topics.title: Clop Extortion Campaign Hits PTC Windchill and FlexPLM
topics.latest_developments: The Clop ransomware gang, also tracked as Cl0p, opened a data-theft extortion campaign against internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle-management instances.
topics.summary: Clop, known for mass exploitation of file-transfer and enterprise software, now steals data from manufacturers' PLM platforms and extorts the owners. Companies running Windchill or FlexPLM should pull them off the public internet and hunt for exfiltration.

sources.title: Clop ransomware targets Windchill, FlexPLM in data theft attacks

topics.title: Laundry Bear Zimbra Flaw Gets CVE-2025-66376
topics.latest_developments: Help Net Security identified the Zimbra Collaboration Suite bug that Russian group Laundry Bear exploits as CVE-2025-66376, the flaw behind the joint NSA, FBI, CISA, Netherlands, UK, Australia, and Canada advisory documenting a campaign that has run since July 2025.
topics.summary: Laundry Bear, also called Void Blizzard, CL-STA-1114, and TA488, breaks into government and commercial networks by exploiting unpatched Zimbra webmail to steal emails. Administrators should patch ZCS immediately.

sources.title: Russian hackers exploit unpatched Zimbra servers to steal emails
